newsitem.title: USA: Generali forms Holocaust policy center.
newsitem.headline: Generali forms Holocaust policy center.

text.p: Italy's largest insurer Assicurazioni Generali SpA plans to announce on Friday the creation of an information center and a toll-free number for the families of Holocaust victims seeking information about insurance policies held by their relatives.
The announcement of the center and 800 number will be made in national advertisements in Friday's New York Times and Los Angeles Times newspapers, Generali said.
Additional advertising will appear in numerous Jewish oriented publications during the coming weeks.
Generali said all available policy information is in the process of being computerized and these records will be made available to the families of policyholders who died in the Holocaust.
Data from the archives also will be provided to Yad Vashem in Jerusalem and the Holocaust Museum in Washington, D.C., to support their efforts to compile names of Holocaust victims, Generali said.
Generali is one of 16 insurers named in a complaint filed earlier this year by Holocaust victims and their families.
The suit claims that individuals who were unable to flee the Nazi persecution were arrested and that their assets, including the insurance policies, were taken by the Nazis.
The policies were then improperly transferred, liquidated or cashed in, the suit alleged.
The Policy Information Center has been established by Generali in the United States and Israel to facilitate the extensive records searches, Generali said.
Individuals contacting the Policy Information Center will be forwarded a policy search request form, Generali said.

They will be instructed to complete the form with as much information as possible about the initial owner of the policy, the approximate date of issue, and the city where the policy would have originated.

After this form is submitted, a search will be initiated in Trieste, Italy. If a match is found, the inquiring family member will receive a copy of the documentation in the archives and any additional information on the status of the policy following World War II, Generali said.
The advertisement appears in the form of an open letter to the families of Holocaust victims, and describes the history of Generali prior to and during the years of World War II, Generali said.
The advertisement also describes the turmoil that faced Generali and many other businesses in post-war Europe, the insurer said.

"The cold-war Communist regimes in Eastern Europe nationalized and expropriated all major businesses, seizing all of Generali's insurance businesses there, including its offices, 184 buildings and 14 companies controlled by Generali," the company said in the advertisement.
"As a result, Generali today has very little information and few records regarding policies issued by its former branches in Central and Eastern Europe," the ad said.
Family members can write or call the Center to request an archival search:
Policy Information Center
45 Rockefeller Plaza
New York, NY 10111-0100
Toll-Free Number: 1-800-456-8174
((Patricia Vowinkel 212-859-1716))
